name: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS)
principle: The product writes upstream input into a web page without neutralizing characters such as '<', '>', and '&'. A browser can interpret attacker-controlled text as script-related HTML and execute code in the user's session.
detection_signals: JSP '<%= request.getParameter(...) %>' or '<%= e.getText() %>' inside an HTML response
Servlet 'out.print(...)' or 'response.getWriter().write(...)' with request parameter, cookie, or header data
C/C++ CGI 'printf("%s", getenv("QUERY_STRING"))' or form data printed after 'Content-Type: text/html'
String concatenation builds '<html>' response with user-controlled variable and no 'escapeHtml' or 'escapeXml' call
Template disables escaping: '<c:out escapeXml="false">', Struts 'filter="false"', or raw triple-stash '{{{x}}}'
User-controlled comment, name, message, filename, or error parameter echoed between HTML tags without entity encoding
HTML response writes user-controlled bytes without explicit charset such as 'Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8'
negative_signals: Output uses HTML body encoder: 'StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml4(x)', 'Encode.forHtml(x)', 'HtmlUtils.htmlEscape(x)', or 'fn:escapeXml(x)'
C/C++ output passes user data through an HTML entity encoder for '&', '<', '>', '"', and '\'' before 'printf' or 'write'
Displayed value is a compile-time constant or server-generated enum with no request, cookie, header, URL, or storage taint
false_defense_traps: Filtering only the substring 'script' is bypassed by case changes or non-script tags
Escaping only '<' but not '&' or '>' leaves entity and parsing bypasses
Validating only visible form fields misses hidden fields, cookies, headers, and URL data later reflected
Setting 'HttpOnly' on cookies reduces cookie theft but does not stop injected script execution
Using a blacklist of tag names instead of context-appropriate HTML entity encoding
verification_focus: Can attacker-controlled request, cookie, header, URL, or stored data reach an HTML response body without entity-encoding '<', '>', and '&'?

consequence_chains.trigger: Unencoded script-related HTML tag is reflected or stored in a generated web page
consequence_chains.consequence: Browser executes attacker-controlled script, enabling session actions, data theft, or page modification

consequence_chains.trigger: Output neutralization is absent or incomplete for HTML metacharacters
consequence_chains.consequence: Special characters are interpreted by the browser as markup instead of data

patch_principle: Apply context-appropriate HTML entity encoding at every HTML output sink.
Use framework auto-escaping templates and do not disable escaping for user data.
Validate all request parts with a positive specification before storage or reflection.
Specify a consistent response charset such as UTF-8 in headers and page metadata.
Use HttpOnly cookies only as defense in depth, not as the XSS fix.
